relevance_reason: Reports a family in which two sisters have autosomal recessive DES-related cardio/myopathy caused by compound heterozygous DES variants, with functional splicing studies.

findings.statement: Riley et al. (2019) described 2 sisters who presented in their twenties with slowly progressive limb-girdle weakness, severe systolic dysfunction, and progressive, severe respiratory weakness. Muscle biopsy showed variation in fiber size with more central nuclei. Electron microscopy showed extensive myofibrillar disarray and duplication of the basal lamina, but no inclusions or aggregates.
quotes: Both sisters presented in their twenties with slowly progressive limb girdle weakness, severe systolic dysfunction, and progressive, severe respiratory weakness.
Biopsy showed fibre size variation with increased central nuclei.
Electron microscopy showed extensive myofibrillar disarray, duplication of the basal lamina, but no inclusions or aggregates.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter

findings.statement: In the 2 affected sisters, Riley et al. (2019) identified compound heterozygous variants in the DES gene: a missense variant, p.(Leu190Pro), inherited from the father, and a deep intronic variant in intron 7, inherited from the mother, that was predicted to create a cryptic splice site. The disease segregated with these variants. The father and brothers who carried only the p.(Leu190Pro) variant were clinically unaffected.
quotes: We establish autosomal recessive DES variants p.(Leu190Pro) and a deep intronic splice variant causing inclusion of a frameshift-inducing artificial exon/intronic fragment, as the likely cause of myopathy with cardiac involvement in female siblings.
a paternal missense p.(Leu190Pro) variant was viewed unlikely to be causative of autosomal dominant desminopathy, as the father and brothers carrying this variant were clinically unaffected.
identifying a maternal deep intronic variant within intron-7, predicted to create a cryptic splice site, which segregated with disease.

findings.statement: Riley et al. (2019) showed by RNA sequencing and analysis of muscle cDNA that the maternal deep intronic DES variant caused aberrant splicing, inserting an artificial exon/intronic fragment into the transcript. This fragment shifted the reading frame and created a premature termination codon. The resulting nonsense-mediated decay was strong, so that 92% of DES transcripts were paternal and 8% were maternal. Western blot showed a 60 to 75% reduction in desmin, which likely consisted only of the p.(Leu190Pro) mutant desmin.
quotes: RNA sequencing and studies of muscle cDNA confirmed the deep intronic variant caused aberrant splicing of an artificial exon/intronic fragment into maternal DES mRNA transcripts, encoding a premature termination codon, and potently activating nonsense-mediate decay (92% paternal DES transcripts, 8% maternal).
Western blot showed 60-75% reduction in desmin levels, likely comprised only of missense p.(Leu190Pro) desmin.

findings.statement: Riley et al. (2019) noted that desminopathy is usually autosomal dominant but that a few autosomal recessive cases have been reported. They concluded that their family widened the phenotypic range of recessive DES cardio/myopathy, here without myofibrillar aggregates.
quotes: Desmin is an intermediate filament protein typically associated with autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy with cardiac involvement. However a few rare cases of autosomal recessive desminopathy are reported.
This study expands the phenotypic spectrum of recessive DES cardio/myopathy

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows a workshop report on reforming limb-girdle muscular dystrophy nomenclature and classification. That context is relevant to the former LGMD1D/LGMD2R names in this entry, but the title gives no desmin-specific details.

findings.statement: Straub et al. (2018) reported on the 229th ENMC international workshop, held in Naarden, the Netherlands, in March 2017, which addressed the nomenclature and a reformed classification of the limb-girdle muscular dystrophies.
quotes: 229th ENMC international workshop: Limb girdle muscular dystrophies - Nomenclature and reformed classification Naarden, the Netherlands, 17-19 March 2017.

relevance_reason: The title reports restrictive cardiomyopathy caused by a novel desmin (DES) mutation, which is relevant to desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy. Only the title was available, so details could not be extracted.

findings.statement: Ojrzyńska et al. (2017) reported restrictive cardiomyopathy caused by a novel mutation in the desmin gene.
quotes: Restrictive cardiomyopathy due to novel desmin gene mutation.

relevance_reason: Reports an autosomal recessive DES splice-site mutation causing an LGMD2 phenotype without myofibrillar myopathy features (the condition formerly called LGMD2R), which falls within the MFM1/desminopathy entry.

findings.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous family in which 2 members had autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD2). LGMD2 is marked by progressive weakness of the proximal shoulder and pelvic girdle muscles. Unlike in autosomal dominant desminopathies, skeletal muscle from the patients did not show ultrastructural changes such as disrupted myofibrillar organization, myofibrillar degradation products, or dislocated or aggregated membranous organelles.
quotes: Here we have investigated a consanguineous family with LGMD2 with two affected individuals in order to identify the causative gene defect.

Unlike autosomal dominant desminopathies, ultrastructural alterations such as disruption of myofibrillar organisation, formation of myofibrillar degradation products and dislocation/aggregation of membranous organelles were not present.

findings.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) used genome-wide homozygosity mapping in this consanguineous family and mapped the LGMD2 phenotype to chromosome 2q35-q36.3.
quotes: We performed genome wide homozygosity mapping and mapped the LGMD2 phenotype to chromosome 2q35-q36.3.

findings.statement: In the 2 affected members of this consanguineous family, Cetin et al. (2013) sequenced the candidate gene DES and found a homozygous splice-site mutation, c.1289-2A>G. The mutation added 16 amino acids to the desmin tail domain, a region that had been suggested to interact with lamin B.
quotes: DNA sequence analysis of the highly relevant candidate gene DES revealed a homozygous splice site mutation c.1289-2A>G in the two affected family members.
This novel splice site mutation results in addition of 16 amino acids within the tail domain of desmin, which has been suggested to interact with lamin B protein.

findings.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) found by immunofluorescence and Western blot analysis that the mutant desmin was still expressed and still formed a cytoskeletal network in patient skeletal muscle fibers. Using confocal laser scanning microscopy, they found a specific disruption of the desmin-lamin B interaction in the patient's skeletal muscle. The authors concluded that autosomal recessive DES mutations cause an LGMD2 phenotype without features of myofibrillar myopathy.
quotes: Immunofluorescent staining and western blot analysis showed that the expression and the cytoskeletal network formation of mutant desmin were well preserved in skeletal muscle fibres.
We also detected a specific disruption of desmin-lamin B interaction in the skeletal muscle of the patient by confocal laser scanning microscopy.
Our study reveals that autosomal recessive mutations in DES cause LGMD2 phenotype without features of myofibrillar myopathy.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a case of desmin cardiomyopathy that began in adolescence and changed from one cardiomyopathy phenotype to another over time. It adds clinical evidence to the desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy entry. No variant details are given in the abstract.

findings.statement: Gudkova et al. (2013) reported what they described as the first case of desmin cardiomyopathy that began in adolescence. Over time the patient's clinical phenotype changed through several types of cardiomyopathy. The authors noted that this made it difficult to diagnose and treat the disease correctly at an early stage.
quotes: This report describes the first case of desmin cardiomyopathy with early manifestation in adolescence and transformation of several clinical phenotypes over time, representing sufficient difficulties for the correct clinical diagnosis and treatment of the disease at an early stage.

findings.statement: Gudkova et al. (2013) noted that desmin cardiomyopathy is a rare cause of congestive heart failure. When it appears in adulthood, it is often associated with conduction disorders and a neuromuscular phenotype. The disease can produce a range of clinical phenotypes, including hypertrophic, restrictive, and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
quotes: Desmin cardiomyopathy is a rare cause of congestive heart failure. Its clinical manifestation in adulthood often is associated with conduction disorders and a neuromuscular phenotype.
However, the disease can result in the variety of clinical phenotypes, including hypertrophic, restrictive, and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

relevance_reason: Identifies a DES mutation as the cause of the autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy with ARVC (formerly ARVD7) in the Swedish family that had previously been linked to 10q22.3.

findings.statement: In a Swedish family with autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), Hedberg et al. (2012) used exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous c.1255C>T transition in the DES gene on chromosome 2q35, resulting in a pro419-to-ser (P419S) substitution. Sanger sequencing of 17 family members confirmed the mutation in 7 of the 10 family members who had been classified as affected in a previous study.
quotes: A heterozygous C-to-T transition, c.1255C>T, p.Pro419Ser in the desmin gene on chromosome 2q35, was identified.
Sanger sequencing of DNA from 17 family members confirmed the heterozygous c.1255C>T desmin mutation in seven out of ten family members that had been classified as affected in the previous study.

findings.statement: Hedberg et al. (2012) noted that the Swedish family with myofibrillar myopathy and ARVC had previously shown linkage to chromosome 10q22.3, but no causative mutation had been found in that region; the causative mutation was instead found in the DES gene on chromosome 2q35.
quotes: Previous studies had demonstrated linkage to chromosome 10q22.3, but no causative mutation had been found in that region.

findings.statement: Hedberg et al. (2012) concluded that some dominantly inherited muscle diseases present diagnostic difficulties because they can display wide clinical and morphologic variability even within a single family.
quotes: the diagnostic difficulties with some forms of dominantly inherited muscle diseases as they can display a wide clinical and morphological variability even within a given family

relevance_reason: The paper identifies a DES splice variant as the cause of the family previously linked to 6q23 as LGMD1D/1E, which reclassifies that disorder as a desminopathy (MFM1).

findings.statement: Greenberg et al. (2012) found that limb girdle muscular dystrophy 1D/1E (LGMD1D/1E), a skeletal and cardiac myopathy previously linked to chromosome 6q23, was caused by a splice donor site mutation in the desmin gene (DES) on chromosome 2q35. They found the mutation (IVS3+3A>G) by sequencing a patient and family members.
quotes: Sequencing in this patient and family members identified the genetic basis of the previously reported 6q23 linked LGMD1D/1E to be due to an intron splice donor site mutation (IVS3+3A>G) of the desmin gene located on chromosome 2q35.

findings.statement: Greenberg et al. (2012) used laser capture microdissection to isolate cytoplasmic inclusions from the skeletal muscle of a patient with LGMD1D/1E. Mass spectrometry-based proteomics and bioinformatic analysis of these inclusions showed that desmin was their major constituent.
quotes: We used laser capture microdissection to isolate cytoplasmic inclusions from skeletal muscle from a patient with LGMD1D/1E, performed mass spectrometry-based proteomics on these minute inclusions, and identified through bioinformatics desmin as their major constituent.

phenotypes.text: cytoplasmic inclusions in skeletal muscle containing desmin

findings.statement: Greenberg et al. (2012) noted that the disorder they studied was named LGMD1D in OMIM nomenclature and LGMD1E by the Human Gene Nomenclature Committee.
quotes: Limb girdle muscular dystrophy 1D/1E (OMIM nomenclature LGMD1D, Human Gene Nomenclature Committee LGMD1E), a skeletal and cardiac myopathy, has previously been linked to chromosome 6q23.

relevance_reason: Review and meta-analysis of 159 DES mutation carriers describing clinical spectrum and genotype-phenotype correlations of desmin-related myopathy.

findings.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) described desmin-related myopathy (DRM) as an autosomally inherited skeletal and cardiac myopathy, mainly caused by dominant mutations in the desmin gene (DES).
quotes: Desmin-related myopathy (DRM) is an autosomally inherited skeletal and cardiac myopathy, mainly caused by dominant mutations in the desmin gene (DES).

findings.statement: In a meta-analysis of 159 reported DES mutation carriers with 40 different mutations, van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) found neurological signs in 74% and cardiological signs in 74% of carriers; 49% had both, 22% had isolated neurological signs, and 22% had isolated cardiological signs. More than 70% had myopathy or muscular weakness, with normal creatine kinase in one-third of them; up to 50% had cardiomyopathy and around 60% had cardiac conduction disease or arrhythmias, with atrioventricular block as an important hallmark.
quotes: DES mutation carriers (n = 159) with 40 different mutations were included. Neurological signs were present in 74% and cardiological signs in 74% of carriers (both neurological and cardiological signs in 49%, isolated neurological signs in 22%, and isolated cardiological signs in 22%).
More than 70% of carriers exhibited myopathy or muscular weakness, with normal creatine kinase levels present in one third of them.
Up to 50% of carriers had cardiomyopathy and around 60% had cardiac conduction disease or arrhythmias, with atrioventricular block as an important hallmark.

findings.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) noted that symptoms generally began in the fourth decade; a quarter of carriers died at a mean age of 49 years, and sudden cardiac death occurred in 2 patients with a pacemaker, suggesting ventricular tachyarrhythmia as the cause of death.
quotes: Symptoms generally started during the 30s; a quarter of carriers died at a mean age of 49 years.
Sudden cardiac death occurred in two patients with a pacemaker, suggesting a ventricular tachyarrhythmia as cause of death.

findings.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) found that most DES mutations were missense mutations, mostly located in the 2B domain. Mutations in the 2B domain predominated in patients with an isolated neurological phenotype, whereas head and tail domain mutations predominated in patients with an isolated cardiological phenotype.
quotes: The majority of DES mutations were missense mutations, mostly located in the 2B domain.

Mutations in the 2B domain were predominant in patients with an isolated neurological phenotype, whereas head and tail domain mutations were predominant in patients with an isolated cardiological phenotype.

relevance_reason: Reports DES mutation families with desmin-related myopathy and right ventricular involvement/ARVC-like phenotype, plus immunohistochemistry of intercalated disk proteins.

findings.statement: Otten et al. (2010) evaluated 2 families carrying different DES mutations. One family was diagnosed with desmin-related myopathy, with an ARVC-like phenotype in 1 patient, whereas the other family presented with severe biventricular cardiomyopathy. The authors concluded that an ARVC-like phenotype or a severe cardiomyopathy with right ventricular involvement are possible, yet infrequent, cardiac phenotypes in desmin-related myopathy.
quotes: One family was diagnosed with DRM, with an ARVC(-like) phenotype in one patient, while the other family presented with a severe biventricular cardiomyopathy.
We confirmed that either an ARVC-like phenotype or a severe cardiomyopathy with right ventricular involvement are possible, yet infrequent, cardiac phenotypes in DRM.

findings.statement: Otten et al. (2010) identified a DES missense mutation, p.N342D, in a family with desmin-related myopathy in which 1 patient had an ARVC-like phenotype.
quotes: Except for two different DES mutations (p.N342D and p.R454W) in two families with DRM and severe biventricular cardiomyopathy, respectively, we did not find additional DES mutations in ARVC(-like) patients.

findings.statement: Otten et al. (2010) identified a DES mutation, p.R454W, in a family with severe biventricular cardiomyopathy. Immunohistochemistry of myocardial tissue from 2 mutation carriers showed desmin aggregates and decreased desmoplakin and plakophilin-2 at the intercalated disk, suggesting a link between desmosomal cardiomyopathies and cardiomyopathies caused by DES mutations.
quotes: In addition to desmin aggregates, immunohistochemistry demonstrated a decreased amount of desmoplakin and plakophilin-2 at the intercalated disk in p.R454W mutation carriers.
suggesting a link between desmosomal cardiomyopathies (mainly affecting the right ventricle) and cardiomyopathies caused by DES mutations

findings.statement: Otten et al. (2010) screened the DES gene in 50 patients with ARVC or ARVC-like phenotypes and found no additional DES mutations, indicating that DES mutations are an infrequent cause of ARVC.
quotes: The DES gene was screened for mutations in 50 ARVC(-like) patients.
we did not find additional DES mutations in ARVC(-like) patients

relevance_reason: Describes 27 patients from 5 families carrying the DES p.S13F founder mutation with desmin-related myopathy/cardiomyopathy, including ARVC phenocopies.

findings.statement: van Tintelen et al. (2009) studied 27 carriers or obligate carriers of a DES p.S13F founder mutation from 5 families, who showed a fully penetrant yet variable phenotype. All patients had cardiac involvement characterized by high-grade AV block at young ages and important right ventricular involvement: right bundle branch block in 10 patients (sometimes as the first manifestation) and right ventricular heart failure in 6, including 2 who fulfilled diagnostic criteria for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy. The authors concluded that the phenotype was predominantly cardiologic, with early conduction disease, right bundle branch block and/or right ventricular tachycardias, and ARVC phenocopies.
quotes: All 27 carriers or obligate carriers of a p.S13F DES founder mutation demonstrated a fully penetrant yet variable phenotype. All patients demonstrated cardiac involvement characterized by high-grade AV block at young ages and important right ventricular (RV) involvement.

RV predominance was demonstrated by the presence of right bundle branch block in 10 patients (sometimes as a first manifestation) and by RV heart failure in 6 patients, including 2 patients who fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for arrhythmogenic RV cardiomyopathy.

patients show a variable yet predominantly cardiologic phenotype characterized by conduction disease at an early age and RV involvement including right bundle branch block and/or RV tachycardias and arrhythmogenic RV cardiomyopathy phenocopies.

phenotypes.text: high-grade AV block at young age

findings.statement: van Tintelen et al. (2009) identified an identical missense mutation in the head domain of desmin, p.S13F, in 27 carriers or obligate carriers from 5 families with desmin-related myopathy; the mutation was a founder mutation and was fully penetrant.
quotes: The purpose of this study was to investigate the clinical and pathologic characteristics of 27 patients from five families with an identical mutation in the head domain region (p.S13F) of desmin.
All 27 carriers or obligate carriers of a p.S13F DES founder mutation demonstrated a fully penetrant yet variable phenotype.

findings.statement: van Tintelen et al. (2009) reported that the DES p.S13F mutation shared by 5 families was a founder mutation.
quotes: All 27 carriers or obligate carriers of a p.S13F DES founder mutation demonstrated a fully penetrant yet variable phenotype.

findings.statement: Because of the clinical overlap with desmosomal cardiomyopathies, van Tintelen et al. (2009) studied intercalated disks in hearts of DES p.S13F carriers and found normal amounts of major desmosomal proteins but more convoluted, elongated intercalated disks with a zigzag appearance. They suggested that a localized effect of desmin on cardiac intercalated disk structure might contribute to pathogenesis.
quotes: Normal amounts of the major desmosomal proteins were found, but the intercalated disks were more convoluted and elongated and had a zigzag appearance.
A localized effect of desmin on the structure of the cardiac intercalated disks might contribute to disease pathogenesis.

relevance_reason: Case report of autosomal recessive desminopathy (myofibrillar myopathy) with infantile-onset cardiomyopathy caused by a homozygous DES in-frame deletion.

findings.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) reported a girl, the only child of consanguineous (uncle-niece) parents, with recurrent syncope from age 6 months, initially attributed to an accessory conduction pathway/Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, followed by progressive syncopal, presyncopal and cyanotic attacks from age 3 years. At age 15 she had a long narrow face, bilateral facial weakness, ptosis, symmetric scapular winging, atrophy of masseter, temporalis, sternocleidomastoid and trunk muscles, pes cavus, mild shoulder girdle and distal limb weakness, hypoactive reflexes, and 2-fold elevated creatine kinase; EMG showed complex repetitive discharges, some myotonic discharges and a myopathic pattern.
quotes: The patient had repetitive episodes of syncope since the age of 6 months which were initially attributed to right posteroseptal accessory conduction pathway and subsequently diagnosed as Wolf-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome.
On examination at the age of 15 years, she had a long-narrow face with bilateral facial weakness, ptosis, symmetrical winging of the scapulae and poor muscle bulk.
The patient’s parents are in a consanguineous marriage (uncle and niece), in which the patient was the only child.

findings.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) found on Holter monitoring of their patient monomorphic and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, QT prolongation and second-degree AV block, requiring an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator and pacemaker; at 18 years she had recurrent ventricular tachyarrhythmias, mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF 45%), right ventricular dilatation, markedly enlarged atria and restrictive cardiomyopathy. Skeletal weakness progressed rapidly, diarrhea, vomiting and weight loss suggested smooth intestinal muscle involvement, and she died of cardiac failure before age 21.
quotes: Twenty-four-hour Holter monitoring revealed monomorphic and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, occasional prolongation of the QT interval and second degree AV block (Figure 1).
The atria were markedly enlarged. Doppler analysis of mitral flow revealed abnormal filling indicative of restrictive cardiomyopathy.

Developing diarrhea, vomiting and weight loss suggested involvement of smooth intestinal muscles. No cardiac or intestinal biopsy was performed at this time due to patient’s further decline. She died from cardiac failure before her 21st birthday.

findings.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) found on deltoid muscle biopsy variation in fiber size and, in more than 90% of fibers, peripheral deposits of homogeneous eosinophilic material that were Congo red positive and strongly desmin-immunoreactive, along with some rimmed vacuoles; electron microscopy showed granulofilamentous material, consistent with myofibrillar myopathy. The inclusions differed from the amorphous patches seen in most patients with dominant or de novo desmin mutations.
quotes: More than 90% of fibers had well-defined peripheral and often multiple deposits of homogeneous eosinophilic material (Figure 3A) that stained different shades of green with Engel trichrome, appeared Congo red positive and was strongly immunoreactive with antibodies to desmin (Figure 3B).

Ultrastructural examination revealed a matrix of granulofilamentous material with amorphous, granular and electron-dense deposits forming a thick reticular network with interspersed, disorganized thin filaments (Figure 3C).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter

findings.statement: In the patient with infantile-onset cardiomyopathy and myofibrillar myopathy, Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) identified a homozygous 21-nucleotide deletion in the DES gene, predicting in-frame loss of 7 amino acids (RARVDVE; p.R173_E179del) in the 1B helix domain, removing a full heptad. Both consanguineous parents were heterozygous and unaffected. The mutation was noted to prevent desmin filament assembly in transfected MCF-7 cells; the same homozygous deletion had previously been reported by Muñoz-Mármol et al. in a severely affected boy.
quotes: identified a homozygous deletion of 21 nucleotides predicting an in-frame loss of 7 amino acids (RARVDVE) from Arg173 through Glu179 (p.R173_E179del) in the 1B helix domain of the desmin molecule.
The patient’s mother and father was each heterozygous for this mutation.

The homozygous p.Arg173_Glu179del mutation prevented assembly of desmin filaments and compromised the ability of desmin to form an intermediate filament network in transiently transfected MCF-7 cells, providing a confirmation of high pathogenic potential.

findings.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) stated that their case was the first exhaustively proven autosomal recessive desminopathy, as heterozygous carrier parents were unaffected; they noted that about 6% of desminopathy patients show autosomal recessive inheritance with childhood onset (average 5 years).
quotes: In about 6% of patients with desminopathy, the inheritance pattern was autosomal recessive; patients with recessive mutations develop the disease in their childhood (average 5 years).
Our observation is the first known case of infantile-onset desmin mutation-associated cardiomyopathy and the first case exhaustively proven to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

findings.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) concluded that patients with desmin-related cardiomyopathy are at high risk of ventricular arrhythmia and should be considered for implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement even before ventricular dysfunction becomes evident.
quotes: The current observation additionally confirms that patients with desmin-related cardiomyopathy are at high risk of developing ventricular arrhythmia and therefore should be considered candidates for AICD implantation even before ventricular dysfunction becomes evident.

relevance_reason: Follow-up linkage study of the Swedish MFM/ARVC7 family that confirms and narrows the critical region on 10q22.3 and excludes candidate genes.

findings.statement: In a follow-up study of the Swedish family with autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC7), which had previously been tentatively mapped to a 10.6-Mb region on 10q22.3 between D10S605 and D10S215, Kuhl et al. (2008) re-examined the linkage with a high-density SNP panel (Affymetrix Human Mapping 10K Array) and confirmed it. They found no other region with significant evidence for linkage and narrowed the critical interval to 4.27 Mb between D10S1645 and D10S1786.
quotes: In a comprehensive follow-up study we re-examined and confirmed the previous linkage data for ARVC7 using a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism marker panel from Affymetrix (Human Mapping 10K Array). No other regions with significant evidence for linkage were discovered.
The critical interval was narrowed down to 4.27 Mbp between D10S1645 and D10S1786.

findings.statement: Kuhl et al. (2008) found that the narrowed region contained 18 candidate genes, 17 of which (RAI17, PPIF, C10ORF56, SFTPA1, SFTPA2, SFTPA1B, SFTPA2B, SFTPD, C10ORF57, PLAC9, ANXA11, MAT1A, DYDC1, DYDC2, C10ORF58, TSPAN14, and SH2D4B) are shared with the CMD1C region. They found no disease-causing mutation in the coding regions of these genes. Sequence analysis also excluded metavinculin (VCL) and ZASP/cypher (LDB3), which lie proximal and distal to the linked region.
quotes: This reduced the total number of candidate genes to 18 of which 17 (RAI17, PPIF, C10ORF56, SFTPA1, SFTPA2, SFTPA1B, SFTPA2B, SFTPD, C10ORF57, PLAC9, ANXA11, MAT1A, DYDC1, DYDC2, C10ORF58, TSPAN14 and SH2D4B) are shared with the CMD1C region. No disease-causing mutation was found in their coding regions.
Moreover, metavinculin (VCL) and ZASP/cypher (LDB3) proximal and distal to this linked region were excluded by sequence analysis.

findings.statement: To search for submicroscopic and intragenic deletions by PCR, Kuhl et al. (2008) generated hybrid cell lines carrying only the affected or only the normal chromosome 10 homolog. All sequence-tagged sites and exons were present on both homologs. The authors speculated that regulatory mutations in 1 of the 18 genes from 10q22.3 cause a heterogeneous spectrum of clinically distinct myodegenerative disorders that affect skeletal and cardiac muscle to variable degrees.
quotes: To search for submicroscopic and intragenic deletions by PCR, we generated hybrid cell lines carrying only the affected or normal chromosome 10 homolog. All sequence tagged sites and exons were present on both homologs.

We speculate that regulatory mutations in 1 of the 18 genes from 10q22.3 are responsible for a heterogenous spectrum of clinically distinct myodegenerative disorders, affecting both skeletal and cardiac muscles to variable degrees.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a new desmin mutation, S13F, in a Chinese family with desmin myopathy and heart block, together with functional expression studies.

findings.statement: Pica et al. (2008) described a Chinese man with desmin myopathy, complete heart block, and mild weakness of the proximal and distal limbs. Family members who carried the mutation had a similar or milder phenotype.
quotes: Desmin myopathy was identified in a Chinese man with complete heart block and mild proximal and distal limb weakness.
Family members carrying the mutation showed a similar or milder phenotype.

findings.statement: Pica et al. (2008) found a novel heterozygous missense mutation, S13F, in the desmin gene in a Chinese man with desmin myopathy and complete heart block. Family members carrying the mutation also had the disorder. The mutation lies at a protein kinase C phosphorylation site within a highly conserved nonapeptide sequence in the head domain of desmin. When the mutant desmin cDNA was expressed in cell lines, it induced large desmin accumulations while a filamentous network was preserved.
quotes: A novel heterozygous missense S13F mutation of the desmin gene was found to be associated with the myopathy.
The mutation is located at a protein kinase-C phosphorylation site within a highly conserved nonapeptide sequence in the head domain of the desmin protein.
Expression of the mutant desmin cDNA in cell lines induced large desmin accumulations associated with preservation of a filamentous network.

relevance_reason: Reports two related Dutch families with desmin-related myopathy caused by a novel DES S13F mutation, with clinical and pathologic description.

findings.statement: Bergman et al. (2007) reported 2 distantly related Dutch families with autosomal dominant desmin-related myopathy affecting 15 family members. The clinical picture was highly heterogeneous, ranging from isolated dilated cardiomyopathy to a more generalized skeletal myopathy with mild respiratory problems. Muscle biopsies showed intracytoplasmic desmin aggregates on desmin and p62 staining.
quotes: We report here on two distantly related Dutch families with autosomal dominant inheritance of desmin-related myopathy affecting 15 family members.
A highly heterogeneous clinical picture is apparent, varying from isolated dilated cardiomyopathy to a more generalised skeletal myopathy and mild respiratory problems.
Morphological analysis of muscle biopsies revealed intracytoplasmic desmin aggregates (desmin and p62 staining).

findings.statement: In affected members of 2 distantly related Dutch families with desmin-related myopathy, Bergman et al. (2007) identified a novel heterozygous missense mutation, S13F, in the head domain of the desmin gene (DES) that cosegregated with the disease phenotype.
quotes: In both families we identified an identical novel pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation, S13F, in the 'head' domain of the desmin gene which cosegregates with the disease phenotype.

findings.statement: Bergman et al. (2007) stressed the importance of analyzing the desmin gene in patients with familial cardiac conduction disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, and/or progressive skeletal myopathy resembling limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
quotes: This article illustrates the importance of analysing the desmin gene in patients with (familial) cardiac conduction disease, dilated cardiomyopathy and/or a progressive skeletal myopathy resembling limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

relevance_reason: The paper reports three new desmin tail-domain variants in patients with myopathy, along with functional assembly studies of seven tail-domain variants. Only the abstract was available, so it gives no patient details.

findings.statement: Bär et al. (2007) reported 3 novel mutations in the non-alpha-helical carboxy-terminal tail domain of desmin (DES) in patients with desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy: c.1325C>T (p.T442I), c.1360C>T (p.R454W), and c.1379G>T (p.S460I).
quotes: Here we report three novel mutations--c.1325C>T (p.T442I), c.1360C>T (p.R454W), and c.1379G>T (p.S460I)--located in desmin's non-alpha-helical carboxy-terminal "tail" domain.

findings.statement: Bär et al. (2007) studied the 3 novel tail mutations and 4 previously described ones (E413K, K449T, I451M, V469M) using in vitro filament assembly and transfected C2C12 myoblasts. All mutants except E413K and R454W assembled into intermediate filaments in vitro, and all except E413K were incorporated into filament arrays in cells. However, viscometric assays showed that filament properties differed significantly from wild-type desmin. When the mutants were coassembled with wild-type desmin, filament formation and filament-filament interactions were severely disturbed, which the authors interpreted as an inherent incompatibility of mutant and wild-type protein.
quotes: Although all but two mutants (p.E413K, p.R454W) assembled into IFs in vitro and all except p.E413K were incorporated into IF arrays in transfected C2C12 cells, filament properties differed significantly from wild-type desmin as revealed by viscometric assembly assays.

Most notably, when coassembled with wild-type desmin, these mutants revealed a severe disturbance of filament-formation competence and filament-filament interactions, indicating an inherent incompatibility of mutant and wild-type protein to form mixed filaments.

findings.statement: Bär et al. (2007) suggested that the various clinical phenotypes caused by desmin tail mutations may reflect altered interactions of the tail domain with different components of the myoblast cytoskeleton. They proposed that this may lead to diminished biomechanical properties and/or altered metabolism of the individual myocyte.
quotes: The various clinical phenotypes observed may reflect altered interactions of desmin's tail domain with different components of the myoblast cytoskeleton leading to diminished biomechanical properties and/or altered metabolism of the individual myocyte.

relevance_reason: Describes a spontaneous canine case of myofibrillar myopathy with desmin accumulation (an animal model); no gene or variant was identified.

findings.statement: Shelton et al. (2004) described a 1-year-old male neutered Australian Shepherd dog with chronic lameness, contractures, and exercise intolerance. The dog had elevated serum creatine kinase, complex repetitive discharges on electromyography, and clinically identified cardiomyopathy. Light and electron microscopy and immunohistochemistry of muscle biopsies showed a myofibrillar myopathy with accumulation of desmin and other proteins. The authors stated that this was the first report of myofibrillar myopathy in the dog.
quotes: A 1-year-old male neutered Australian Shepherd dog was referred to a veterinary specialist for evaluation of chronic lameness, contractures, and exercise intolerance.
Serum creatine kinase was elevated, and electromyography showed complex repetitive discharges. Cardiomyopathy was clinically identified.
Muscle biopsies evaluated by light and electron microscopy, and immunohistochemistry revealed the presence of a myofibrillar myopathy with accumulation of desmin and other proteins.

relevance_reason: Abstract reports that a recessive desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions is caused by SEPN1 mutations, not desmin. For the desmin-related MFM1 entry, it is useful only as evidence of genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Ferreiro et al. (2004) noted that desmin-related myopathies (DRMs) are a heterogeneous group of muscle disorders defined by intrasarcoplasmic desmin aggregates, and that mutations in the desmin and alpha-B crystallin genes account for approximately one-third of DRM cases.
quotes: Desmin-related myopathies (DRMs) are a heterogeneous group of muscle disorders, morphologically defined by intrasarcoplasmic aggregates of desmin.
Mutations in the desmin and the alpha-B crystallin genes account for approximately one third of the DRM cases.

findings.statement: Ferreiro et al. (2004) found that, in the original German family with early-onset recessive desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions (MB-DRM), the disease was linked to the SEPN1 locus on 1p36. Affected patients had a homozygous 92-nucleotide SEPN1 deletion (del 92 nucleotide -19/+73). The authors reported that MB-DRM shares identical clinical features with SEPN-related myopathy and proposed that it be classified as SEPN-related myopathy. They said these findings substantiated the molecular heterogeneity of DRM.
quotes: In the original MB-DRM German family, we demonstrated a linkage of the disease to the SEPN1 locus (1p36), and subsequently a homozygous SEPN1 deletion (del 92 nucleotide -19/+73) in the affected patients.
Therefore, we propose that MB-DRM should be categorized as SEPN-RM. These findings substantiate the molecular heterogeneity of DRM

relevance_reason: A large MFM cohort (63 patients) that included desmin mutation screening; 4 patients had desmin missense mutations, adding evidence about desmin-related MFM and showing that MFM is genetically heterogeneous. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Selcen et al. (2004) reviewed 63 unrelated patients diagnosed with myofibrillar myopathy at the Mayo Clinic between 1977 and 2003. Mean age at onset was 54 +/- 16 years. Weakness was both proximal and distal in 77% of patients and proximal only in 13%, and cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 16%. EMG showed a myopathic pattern with abnormal electrical irritability. Thirteen patients had abnormal nerve conduction studies, but 4 of these had long-standing diabetes.
quotes: We here review the clinical, structural and genetic features of 63 unrelated patients diagnosed as having MFM at the Mayo Clinic between 1977 and 2003. The age of onset was 54 +/- 16 years (mean +/- SD).
Weakness was both proximal and distal in 77% and proximal only in 13%. Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 16%.
Electro myography revealed a myopathic pattern associated with abnormal electrical irritability; 13 patients had abnormal nerve conduction studies but four of these had long-standing diabetes.

phenotypes.text: myopathic EMG with abnormal electrical irritability

findings.statement: In the 63 patients studied by Selcen et al. (2004), trichrome-stained sections showed abnormal muscle fibers containing amorphous, granular or pleomorphic hyaline structures, which were strongly congophilic, as well as vacuoles containing membranous material. Electron microscopy showed progressive myofibrillar degeneration beginning at the Z-disk, accumulation of degraded filamentous material, and dislocated membranous organelles trapped in autophagic vacuoles.
quotes: The abnormal muscle fibres are best identified in trichrome-stained sections as harbouring amorphous, granular or pleomorphic hyaline structures, and vacuoles containing membranous material. The hyaline structures are strongly congophilic.

Electron microscopy shows progressive myofibrillar degeneration commencing at the Z-disk, accumulation of degraded filamentous material and entrapment of dislocated membranous organelles in autophagic vacuoles.

findings.statement: Selcen et al. (2004) used semiquantitative immunostaining and found that, on average, 90% of abnormal fibers abnormally expressed myotilin, 75% desmin, 75% alpha-B-crystallin, 70% dystrophin and 70% beta-amyloid precursor protein. They concluded that immunostains for these proteins, especially myotilin, are useful adjuncts in diagnosing MFM.
quotes: Semiquantitative analysis in each case indicates that among the abnormal fibres, an average of 90, 75, 75, 70 and 70% abnormally express myotilin, desmin, alphaBC, dystrophin and beta-amyloid precursor protein, respectively.
Therefore, immunostains for these proteins, and especially for myotilin, are useful adjuncts in the diagnosis of MFM.

findings.statement: Selcen et al. (2004) screened 63 unrelated patients with MFM for mutations in desmin, alpha-B-crystallin, telethonin and syncoilin. Four patients carried missense mutations in the head or tail region of desmin (DES), and 2 carried truncating mutations in the C-terminal domain of alpha-B-crystallin (CRYAB). No patient had a mutation in syncoilin or telethonin.
quotes: Two of the 63 patients carry truncation mutations in the C-terminal domain of alphaBC, four carry missense mutations in the head or tail region of desmin, and none carries a mutation in syncoilin or telethonin.

findings.statement: Only 6 of 63 MFM patients had mutations in desmin or alpha-B-crystallin. Selcen et al. (2004) therefore concluded that MFM is morphologically distinct but genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: Thus, MFM is morphologically distinct but genetically heterogeneous.

relevance_reason: The paper reports new in-frame DES deletions found in families with skeletal or cardioskeletal desmin-related myopathy, and it includes structural and expression studies of those deletions.

findings.statement: Kaminska et al. (2004) studied 3 families with skeletal or cardioskeletal myopathy caused by small in-frame deletions in the desmin gene. They described desminopathy as a disease characterized by progressive limb muscle weakness and by desmin-reactive granular aggregates that accumulate in the myofibers.
quotes: We have studied three families with skeletal or cardioskeletal myopathy caused by small in-frame deletions in the desmin gene.
a disease characterized by progressive limb muscle weakness and accumulation of desmin-reactive granular aggregates in the myofibers

findings.statement: In patients with desmin-related myopathy, Kaminska et al. (2004) identified a new in-frame deletion in the DES gene, E359_S361del. It changes the heptad periodicity of the 2B coiled-coil segment. Structural analysis showed that the deletion adds a second stutter immediately downstream of the naturally occurring stutter, which doubles the extent of local coiled-coil unwinding. In expression studies in 2 cell lines, the mutant desmin could not polymerize into a functional filamentous network.
quotes: The newly identified in-frame deletions E359_S361del and N366del alter the heptad periodicity within a critical 2B coiled-coil segment.

Structural analysis reveals that the E359_S361 deletion introduces a second stutter immediately downstream of the naturally occurring stutter, thus doubling the extent of the local coiled-coil unwinding.
Expression studies in two cell lines confirm the inability of desmin molecules with this changed architecture to polymerize into a functional filamentous network.

findings.statement: In patients with desmin-related myopathy, Kaminska et al. (2004) identified a new in-frame deletion in the DES gene, N366del. It changes the heptad periodicity of the 2B coiled-coil segment and turns the wild-type stutter into a stammer, which the authors expected to cause extra overwinding of the coiled coil. In expression studies in 2 cell lines, the mutant desmin could not polymerize into a functional filamentous network.
quotes: The N366del mutation converts the wild-type stutter into a different type of discontinuity, a stammer.
A stammer, as opposed to a stutter, is expected to cause an extra overwinding of the coiled-coil.
Expression studies in two cell lines confirm the inability of desmin molecules with this changed architecture to polymerize into a functional filamentous network.

findings.statement: Kaminska et al. (2004) concluded that small in-frame deletions in the 2B coiled-coil segment of desmin change the coiled-coil geometry in specific ways. They proposed that this causes fatal damage to desmin filament assembly, leading to breakdown of muscle cells and to skeletal or cardioskeletal myopathy.
quotes: These mutations alter the coiled-coil geometry in specific ways leading to fatal damage to desmin filament assembly.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It names a 2002 ENMC workshop on what causes the non-sarcoglycan limb-girdle muscular dystrophies. The title states nothing specific about desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy, so the paper can only give context, possibly about the former LGMD names for MFM1.
The paper reports new DES splice site mutations in two unrelated patients with desmin-related cardiac and skeletal myopathy, plus functional studies of the variants.

findings.statement: Park et al. (2000) identified a heterozygous de novo A-to-G change at the +3 position of the intron 3 splice donor site of the DES gene (IVS3+3A-G) in a patient with sporadic skeletal and cardiac myopathy. They found it by sequencing cDNA and genomic DNA. When they expressed genomic DNA fragments carrying the mutation, the result was deletion of exon 3.
quotes: Sequencing of cDNA and genomic DNA identified a heterozygous de novo A to G change at the +3 position of the splice donor site of intron 3 (IVS3+3A-->G) in a patient with sporadic skeletal and cardiac myopathy.
Expression of genomic DNA fragments carrying the IVS3+3A-->G and IVS2-1G-->A mutations confirmed that these mutations cause exon 3 deletion.

findings.statement: Park et al. (2000) identified a G-to-A transition at the -1 position of the intron 2 splice acceptor site of the DES gene (IVS2-1G-A) in a second, unrelated patient with a similar skeletal and cardiac myopathy. When they expressed genomic DNA fragments carrying the mutation, the result was deletion of exon 3.
quotes: A G to A transition at the highly conserved -1 nucleotide position of intron 2 affecting the splice acceptor site (IVS2-1G-->A) was found in an unrelated patient with a similar phenotype.
Expression of genomic DNA fragments carrying the IVS3+3A-->G and IVS2-1G-->A mutations confirmed that these mutations cause exon 3 deletion.

findings.statement: Park et al. (2000) found that both splice mutations caused skipping of exon 3, giving an in-frame deletion of 32 codons. They predicted that the mutant desmin would lack 32 amino acids from the 1B segment of the alpha-helical rod. When the mutant desmin was expressed in vimentin-deficient SW13 cells, abnormal coarse clumps of desmin-positive material aggregated throughout the cytoplasm.
quotes: Aberrant splicing leads to an in frame deletion of 32 complete codons and is predicted to result in mutant desmin lacking 32 amino acids from the 1B segment of the alpha helical rod.
Functional analysis of the mutant desmin in SW13 (vim-) cells showed aggregation of abnormal coarse clumps of desmin positive material dispersed throughout the cytoplasm.

findings.statement: Park et al. (2000) described desmin myopathy as a hereditary or sporadic cardiac and skeletal myopathy characterized by desmin-reactive deposits that accumulate inside the cytoplasm of muscle cells.
quotes: Desmin myopathy is a hereditary or sporadic cardiac and skeletal myopathy characterised by intracytoplasmic accumulation of desmin reactive deposits in muscle cells.

relevance_reason: Describes the original Swedish family with autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy with ARVC and maps the disorder to 10q22.3.

findings.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) studied a Swedish family with myopathy and cardiomyopathy. They investigated 21 family members neurologically and cardiologically and reviewed the charts of 2 deceased affected patients. Twelve patients had myopathy. Weakness was axial in mildly affected patients, axial and predominantly distal in moderately affected patients, and generalized in severely affected patients. Electromyography showed myopathic signs in 10 patients.
quotes: Twenty-one members of a Swedish family suffering from myopathy and cardiomyopathy underwent neurological and cardiological investigations.
Twelve patients had myopathy. The distribution of weakness was axial in mildly affected, axial and predominantly distal in moderately affected, and generalized in severely affected patients.
The electromyogram showed signs of myopathy in 10 patients.

findings.statement: In this Swedish family, Melberg et al. (1999) found that muscle biopsies showed myopathic changes, rimmed vacuoles, and accumulation of desmin, dystrophin, and other proteins. Electron microscopy showed granulofilamentous changes and disorganized myofibrils.
quotes: Muscle biopsy specimens showed myopathic changes, rimmed vacuoles, and accumulation of desmin, dystrophin, and other proteins.
Electron microscopy revealed granulofilamentous changes and disorganization of myofibrils.

findings.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) reported that several members of the family had episodes of chest pain or palpitations. Three men had arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, with documented nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, atrial flutter, and ventricular dilatation affecting mainly the right ventricle. Two of the 3 men received pacemakers for atrioventricular block and sick sinus syndrome.
quotes: Several patients had episodes of chest pain or palpitations. Three men had arrhythmogenic right ventribular cardiomyopathy.
Nonsustained ventribular tachycardia, atrial flutter, and dilatation of the ventricles mainly affecting the right ventricle were documented.
Two of them had a pacemaker implanted because of atrioventricular block and sick sinus syndrome.

findings.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) concluded that the disorder in this Swedish family was inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, with variable onset and severity of both skeletal muscle and cardiac involvement.
quotes: Inheritance is autosomal dominant with variable onset and severity of skeletal muscle and cardiac involvement.

findings.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) performed linkage analysis of candidate chromosomal regions in this Swedish family. They found a maximum 2-point LOD score of 2.76 at marker D10S1752 on 10q and a multipoint peak LOD score of 3.06 between markers D10S605 and D10S215. They suggested that 10q22.3 may harbor the genetic defect for myofibrillar myopathy with ARVC.
quotes: Linkage analysis of candidate chromosomal regions showed a maximum 2-point LOD score of 2.76 for marker locus D10S1752 on chromosome 10q.
A multipoint peak LOD score of 3.06 between markers D10S605 and D10S215 suggests linkage to chromosome 10q22.3

relevance_reason: Linkage mapping of an autosomal dominant distal myopathy with desmin accumulation and cardiomyopathy to 2q33, a region containing the desmin gene; the abstract does not report any variant.

findings.statement: Saavedra-Matiz et al. (2000) studied a large family with an autosomal dominant hereditary distal myopathy. The myopathy progressed slowly, began in early adulthood in the distal leg muscles, and caused a gait disturbance. Most affected family members also had cardiomyopathy, presenting as conduction block or congestive heart failure. On histology, desmin had accumulated in the subsarcolemmal spaces of myofibers.
quotes: This slowly progressive myopathy begins during early adulthood in the distal leg muscles, producing a gait disturbance.
Cardiomyopathy is also present in most affected family members, manifesting itself as conduction block or congestive heart failure.
Histologically, an accumulation of the protein, desmin, occurs in the subsarcolemmal spaces of myofibers.

findings.statement: In this large family, Saavedra-Matiz et al. (2000) used linkage analysis to map the disease gene to chromosome 2q33. The gene lay within a 17-cM segment bounded by the markers D2S2248 and D2S401. The authors considered desmin the best candidate gene.
quotes: We have performed linkage analyses of this family, and have mapped the location of the gene causing the myopathy to human chromosome 2q33.
The gene is within a 17-cM segment of chromosome 2q bounded by the DNA markers D2S2248 and D2S401.
The best candidate gene for this myopathy is desmin.

relevance_reason: Reports a DES missense mutation (L345P) cosegregating with autosomal dominant desmin-related distal myopathy in a large family, with functional evidence of a dominant-negative effect on filament assembly.

findings.statement: Sjöberg et al. (1999) studied a large 6-generation Ashkenazi Jewish family with autosomal dominant desmin-related myopathy of distal onset.
quotes: The L345P desmin missense mutation occurs in a large, six generation Ashkenazi Jewish family.
In some myopathies of distal onset, the intermediate filament desmin is abnormally accumulated in skeletal and cardiac muscle.

findings.statement: In affected members of a large 6-generation Ashkenazi Jewish family with autosomal dominant distal desmin-related myopathy, Sjöberg et al. (1999) identified a heterozygous L345P missense mutation in the DES gene that cosegregated with the disease; it was the first point mutation in desmin reported to cosegregate with autosomal dominant desmin-related myopathy. The mutation lies at an evolutionarily highly conserved position of the coiled-coil rod domain important for dimer formation.
quotes: We report the first point mutation in desmin cosegregating with an autosomal dominant form of desmin-related myopathy.
The mutation is located in an evolutionarily highly conserved position of the desmin coiled-coil rod domain important for dimer formation.

findings.statement: Sjöberg et al. (1999) found that L345P desmin was incapable of forming filamentous networks in transfected HeLa and SW13 cells, and concluded that the mutation causes myopathy by interfering in a dominant-negative manner with the dimerization-polymerization process of intermediate filament assembly.
quotes: L345P desmin is incapable of forming filamentous networks in transfected HeLa and SW13 cells.
We conclude that the L345P desmin missense mutation causes myopathy by interfering in a dominant-negative manner with the dimerization-polymerization process of intermediate filament assembly.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a patient with desmin-related myopathy caused by a DES in-frame deletion, with functional evidence that the mutant protein does not assemble properly.

findings.statement: Muñoz-Mármol et al. (1998) reported a patient with severe generalized myopathy. The patient's muscle showed abnormal accumulation of desmin intermediate filaments within the sarcoplasm.
quotes: We report here a human patient with severe generalized myopathy and aberrant intrasarcoplasmic accumulation of desmin intermediate filaments.

phenotypes.text: intrasarcoplasmic accumulation of desmin intermediate filaments

findings.statement: In muscle tissue from a patient with severe generalized myopathy, Muñoz-Mármol et al. (1998) found a DES mutation encoding a 7-amino acid deletion within the coiled-coil segment of desmin. The wildtype desmin allele was absent from the patient's muscle. Recombinant desmin carrying this deletion did not form proper desmin intermediate filament networks in cultured cells and did not assemble into 10-nm filaments in vitro.
quotes: Muscle tissue from this patient lacks the wild-type desmin allele and has a desmin gene mutation encoding a 7-aa deletion within the coiled-coil segment of the protein.
We show that recombinant desmin harboring this deletion cannot form proper desmin intermediate filament networks in cultured cells, nor is it able to assemble into 10-nm filaments in vitro.

findings.statement: Muñoz-Mármol et al. (1998) concluded that their findings were direct evidence that a desmin mutation can cause human myopathy. They noted that desmin-null mice form muscle fibers with Z disks and normal sarcomeres, but these muscles are mechanically fragile and degenerate with repeated contraction.
quotes: These findings provide direct evidence that a mutation in desmin can cause human myopathies.
Mice lacking desmin produce muscle fibers with Z disks and normal sarcomeric organization. However, the muscles are mechanically fragile and degenerate upon repeated contractions.

relevance_reason: Reports DES mutations in two families with desmin-related cardioskeletal myopathy, establishing the molecular basis of MFM1.

findings.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) described desmin-related myopathy as a familial disorder characterized by skeletal muscle weakness associated with cardiac conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and restrictive heart failure, and by intracytoplasmic accumulation of desmin-reactive deposits in cardiac and skeletal muscle cells.
quotes: Desmin-related myopathy (OMIM 601419) is a familial disorder characterized by skeletal muscle weakness associated with cardiac conduction blocks, arrhythmias and restrictive heart failure, and by intracytoplasmic accumulation of desmin-reactive deposits in cardiac and skeletal muscle cells.

findings.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) noted that involvement of the desmin gene (DES) had been excluded in 3 families diagnosed with desmin-related myopathy.
quotes: Involvement of the desmin gene (DES) has been excluded in three families diagnosed with desmin-related myopathy.

findings.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) reported 2 families with desmin-related cardioskeletal myopathy: one with adult-onset skeletal myopathy and mild cardiac involvement, and a second characterized by a childhood-onset aggressive course of cardiac and skeletal myopathy.
quotes: A heterozygous A337P mutation was identified in a family with an adult-onset skeletal myopathy and mild cardiac involvement.
a second family characterized by childhood-onset aggressive course of cardiac and skeletal myopathy.

phenotypes.text: childhood-onset aggressive cardiac and skeletal myopathy

findings.statement: In a family with adult-onset skeletal myopathy and mild cardiac involvement, Goldfarb et al. (1998) identified a heterozygous A337P mutation in the highly conserved carboxy-terminal end of the desmin rod domain.
quotes: A heterozygous A337P mutation was identified in a family with an adult-onset skeletal myopathy and mild cardiac involvement.
mutations in the highly conserved carboxy-terminal end of the desmin rod domain

findings.statement: In a family with childhood-onset aggressive cardiac and skeletal myopathy, Goldfarb et al. (1998) detected compound heterozygosity for 2 DES mutations, A360P and N393I, in the carboxy-terminal end of the desmin rod domain.
quotes: Compound heterozygosity for two other mutations, A360P and N393I, was detected in a second family characterized by childhood-onset aggressive course of cardiac and skeletal myopathy.

relevance_reason: The abstract reviews how five distal myopathies (Welander, Markesbery-Griggs/Udd, Nonaka, Miyoshi, Laing) are classified clinically and genetically. It does not mention desmin, myofibrillar myopathy or cardiomyopathy, so it gives context only for MFM1, and no finding specific to MFM1 can be backed by quotes from it.
Original description and mapping of FDC with conduction defect and muscular dystrophy (CMD1F/LGMD1D), a former designation folded into MFM1.

findings.statement: Messina et al. (1997) characterized an autosomal dominant disorder involving dilated cardiomyopathy, cardiac conduction-system disease, and adult-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, which they called FDC-CDM (familial dilated cardiomyopathy, conduction disease, and myopathy).
quotes: We now characterize an autosomal dominant disorder involving dilated cardiomyopathy, cardiac conduction-system disease, and adult-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (FDC, conduction disease, and myopathy [FDC-CDM]).

findings.statement: By genomewide scan, Messina et al. (1997) identified a region on chromosome 6q significantly linked to the myopathy in FDC-CDM (maximum lod score 4.99 at theta = 0.00 for D6S262). Haplotype analysis refined the interval to 3 cM between D6S1705 and D6S1656, excluding striated muscle-expressed genes in the region including laminin alpha-2, laminin alpha-4, triadin, and phospholamban.
quotes: A genomewide scan identified a region on the long arm of chromosome 6 that is significantly associated with the presence of myopathy (D6S262; maximum LOD score [Z(max)] 4.99 at maximum recombination fraction [theta(max)] .00), identifying FDC-CDM as a genetically distinct disease.

Haplotype analysis refined the interval containing the genetic defect, to a 3-cM interval between D6S1705 and D6S1656. This haplotype analysis excludes a number of striated muscle-expressed genes present in this region, including laminin alpha2, laminin alpha4, triadin, and phospholamban.

findings.statement: Messina et al. (1997) used linkage to exclude genomic regions known to be linked to dilated cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy phenotypes, confirming genetic heterogeneity and identifying FDC-CDM as genetically distinct.
quotes: Genetic linkage was used to exclude regions of the genome known to be linked to dilated cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy phenotypes and to confirm genetic heterogeneity of these disorders.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a family (two siblings) with cardiomyopathy and progressive myopathy in which desmin builds up in muscle. This is the desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy phenotype.

findings.statement: Vajsar et al. (1993) reported 2 sibs who developed cardiomyopathy several years before the onset of slowly progressive muscle weakness. The authors concluded that these clinical and pathologic features characterized a rare familial myopathy associated with an unusual distribution of desmin intermediate filament proteins in skeletal and probably also cardiac muscle.
quotes: Two siblings developed cardiomyopathy several years before slowly progressive muscle weakness.

These clinical and pathological features characterise a rare familial myopathy associated with an unusual distribution of desmin intermediate filament proteins in skeletal and probably also cardiac muscle.

findings.statement: In the 2 sibs, Vajsar et al. (1993) found subsarcolemmal crescents of dark eosinophilic material in both type I and type II fibers on skeletal muscle biopsy. This material stained for desmin and ubiquitin but for no other cytoskeletal proteins. On electron microscopy, the deposits were aggregates of granular and filamentous material arising from Z-bands. Follow-up biopsies 6 years later showed more fibers containing desmin- and ubiquitin-positive subsarcolemmal aggregates.
quotes: Skeletal muscle biopsy specimens showed subsarcolemmal crescents of dark eosinophilic material in both type I and type II fibres.
Immunohistochemically the subsarcolemmal material stained positively for the intermediate filament protein desmin and for the heat shock protein ubiquitin but for no other cytoskeletal proteins.

Ultrastructurally the subsarcolemmal deposits consisted of aggregates of granular and filamentous material arising from Z-bands. Follow up muscle biopsies six years later showed an increased number of the muscle fibres that contained subsarcolemmal aggregates that stained positively for desmin and ubiquitin.

phenotypes.text: subsarcolemmal desmin-positive aggregates in muscle fibers

relevance_reason: Clinical and pathologic description of an autosomal dominant cytoplasmic body myopathy kindred (a desmin-related/myofibrillar myopathy phenotype) with cardiac and respiratory involvement; no molecular data.

findings.statement: Abe et al. (1993) described a Japanese kindred with autosomal dominant progressive myopathy with diffuse cytoplasmic bodies, in which 12 patients across 4 successive generations had weakness and atrophy of muscles of the distal extremities, neck, thorax, and shoulder girdles. Mean age at onset was 42 years, and patients became disabled after 5 to 10 years due to chronic respiratory failure. Serum creatine kinase was normal or slightly elevated, and EMG showed predominantly myopathic changes with slight neurogenic change. Males were more frequently affected than females (2:1).
quotes: In four successive generations, 12 patients suffered from weakness and atrophy of muscles in the distal extremities, neck, thorax and shoulder girdles.
The mean age at onset was 42 years old, and the patients became disabled after 5 to 10 years due to chronic respiratory failure.
The level of serum creatine kinase was normal or slightly elevated. An electromyogram showed a predominant myopathic change with a slight neurogenic change.

phenotypes.text: normal or slightly elevated serum creatine kinase
myopathic EMG with slight neurogenic change

findings.statement: Abe et al. (1993) reported that autopsy of 2 affected members of the kindred revealed numerous cytoplasmic bodies in skeletal muscle, predominantly in type I fibers, with smooth and cardiac muscle also affected. Electron microscopy showed dense central cores of myofilaments surrounded by radiating filaments.
quotes: Autopsy of 2 cases revealed numerous CBs in the skeletal muscles. Smooth and cardiac muscles were also affected. CBs were present predominantly in type I fibers in skeletal muscles.
An electron microscopic examination showed dense central cores of myofilaments surrounded by radiating filaments.

findings.statement: Abe et al. (1993) observed autosomal dominant inheritance of cytoplasmic body myopathy through 4 successive generations of a Japanese kindred.
quotes: An autosomal dominant progressive myopathy with diffuse cytoplasmic bodies (CBs) is described.
In four successive generations, 12 patients suffered

relevance_reason: This paper describes a large family with autosomal dominant distal myopathy, desmin storage and cardiac involvement. These are the clinicopathologic features of desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy.

findings.statement: Horowitz and Schmalbruch (1994) described a large kindred with autosomal dominant distal myopathy. Onset was in early to middle adulthood with gait disturbance due to distal leg weakness. Over 5 to 10 years the disease progressed to involve all extremities and the bulbar, respiratory and facial muscles. Cardiac involvement was frequent, with arrhythmias, conduction blocks and congestive heart failure, and led to premature death.
quotes: The disease begins in early to middle adulthood with gait disturbance due to distal leg weakness, and progresses over 5-10 years to involve all extremities, as well as bulbar, respiratory, and facial muscles.
There is frequent cardiac involvement, manifest by arrhythmias, conduction blocks, and congestive failure, resulting in premature demise.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: In the family reported by Horowitz and Schmalbruch (1994), electromyography showed prominent spontaneous activity, short-duration motor unit potentials and polyphasia. Muscle biopsies from several family members at different stages of the disease showed desmin storage and autophagocytosis. The authors noted that this distal myopathy differed from other phenotypically similar disorders in its rapid progression, fatal course and pathologic features.
quotes: On electromyography there is prominent spontaneous activity, short duration motor unit potentials, and polyphasia.
Muscle biopsies from multiple family members at different stages of the disease are characterized by desmin storage and autophagocytosis.
This distal myopathy differs from other phenotypically similar disorders in its rapidity of progression, fatal course and pathologic features.

phenotypes.text: myopathic EMG with spontaneous activity, short-duration motor unit potentials and polyphasia

relevance_reason: A case report of desmin myopathy with involvement of skeletal, cardiac and intestinal smooth muscle. It widens the range of desmin-related myopathy (MFM1), but no molecular data are given.

findings.statement: Ariza et al. (1995) described a 28-year-old man with desmin myopathy who had generalized muscular atrophy, cardiomyopathy, and intestinal malabsorption and pseudo-obstruction. The authors stated that this was the first report of intestinal smooth muscle involvement in desmin myopathy, in addition to its known skeletal and cardiac muscle features.
quotes: The present study focuses on a 28-year-old man with generalized muscular atrophy, cardiomyopathy, and intestinal malabsorption and pseudo-obstruction.
which in this instance first adds intestinal smooth muscle involvement to its already known skeletal and cardiac muscle manifestations

findings.statement: In the patient described by Ariza et al. (1995), pathologic study found abundant granular and filamentous aggregates in the sarcoplasm that stained strongly for desmin. These aggregates were present throughout the skeletal muscle, the myocardium, and the smooth muscle of the intestine. On electron microscopy, the aggregates were continuous with Z lines or dense bodies. The authors also found axonal spheroids that stained for neurofilament in the spinal cord and roots, which they called an extremely rare combination of intermediate filament pathology in the neuromuscular system.
quotes: Abundant sarcoplasmic granular and filamentous aggregates that were ultrastructurally continuous with Z lines or dense bodies and exhibited intense immunostaining for desmin were present throughout the skeletal musculature, myocardium, and smooth muscle of the intestine.
Moreover, neurofilament-immunoreactive axonal spheroids were identified in the spinal cord and roots.

phenotypes.text: desmin-immunoreactive sarcoplasmic aggregates in skeletal muscle
desmin aggregates in intestinal smooth muscle
axonal spheroids in spinal cord and roots

relevance_reason: Review of desmin pathology in neuromuscular disorders, including families with myopathy and/or cardiomyopathy showing desmin accumulation; abstract only, no patients or variants.

findings.statement: In a review, Goebel (1995) stated that desmin pathology in human neuromuscular disorders always takes the form of increased amounts of desmin, either diffuse or focal. Focal accumulation occurs in two forms: with certain inclusion bodies (cytoplasmic and spheroid bodies), and as patchier granulofilamentous material. Both lesions had been found in certain families affected by a myopathy and/or cardiomyopathy. Other proteins, such as dystrophin, vimentin, actin, ubiquitin, and alpha-B crystallin, may also be overexpressed.
quotes: The pathology of desmin in human neuromuscular disorders is always marked by increased amounts, diffusely or focally.

Focal accretion of desmin may be twofold, in conjunction with certain inclusion bodies, cytoplasmic and spheroid bodies, and in a more patchy fashion, granulofilamentous material. Both lesions have been found in certain families, affected by a myopathy and/or cardiomyopathy.
Other proteins, e.g., dystrophin, vimentin, actin, ubiquitin, and alpha-B crystallin, may also be overexpressed.

findings.statement: Goebel (1995) suggested that desmin pathology may be genetically regulated, or may simply reflect severely impaired metabolism of several proteins within muscle fibers.
quotes: Desmin pathology may be genetically regulated or may merely reflect profoundly impaired metabolism of several proteins within myofibers.

relevance_reason: Early clinicopathologic report of a familial cardiomyopathy with storage of intermediate (desmin-type) filaments. The authors suggest a disturbance in desmin metabolism, which is the basis of desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy.

findings.statement: Porte et al. (1980) described 3 brothers with progressive myocardial deficiency. On histology, most cardiac muscle cells showed massive storage of PAS-negative proteinaceous material. Electron microscopy showed that this material consisted of sinuous filaments 7 to 10 nm in diameter, similar to intermediate filaments. Filament storage coincided with disintegration of neighbouring myofibrils. Z-band changes gave rise to rod-like bodies, and Z-band material associated with sarcoplasmic reticulum tubules formed more complex structures.
quotes: Unusual histological and ultrastructural changes in cardiac muscle cells have been found in 3 brothers with progressive myocardial deficiency.
Histologically, this cardiomyopathy was characterized by massive storage of PAS-negative proteinaceous material in most cardiac muscle cells.
The electron microscope showed that this material consisted of sinuous filaments, 7-10 nm in diameter, similar to the intermediate filaments normally present in cardiac muscle cells.

phenotypes.text: intermediate filament storage in cardiac muscle cells
rod-like bodies derived from Z bands

findings.statement: Porte et al. (1980) found that, in the 3 brothers, filament storage and myofibrillar disintegration always occurred in areas of extensive development and involution of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, together with relatively high glycogen accumulation. A few skeletal muscle fibers also showed discrete sarcoplasmic reticulum proliferation, glycogen overload and filament deposits.
quotes: Filament storage and myofibrillar disintegration always occurred in areas where the SR developed and involuted extensively.
Relatively high glycogen accumulation also occurred, in close relation to the SR changes.
Discrete SR proliferation, glycogen overload and filament deposits were observed in a few skeletal fibres.

phenotypes.text: filament deposits in skeletal muscle fibers

findings.statement: Porte et al. (1980) suggested that a disturbance in the metabolism of desmin might be involved in this cardiomyopathy. They described desmin as the protein subunit of intermediate filaments and a fundamental component of Z bands. Because of the marked sarcoplasmic reticulum abnormalities, they also suggested that a chronic defect in calcium regulation might play a role.
quotes: These observations suggest that disturbance in the metabolism of desmin (protein subunit of intermediate filaments and a fundamental component of Z bands) might be involved in this type of cardiomyopathy.
The influence of a chronic defect in calcium regulation might also be envisaged in view of the marked SR abnormalities.

relevance_reason: The title describes a familial cardiomyopathy with abnormal build-ups of desmin-type intermediate filaments, which is an early description of desmin-related myopathy. Only the title was available, so no further detail could be taken from the paper.

findings.statement: Stoeckel et al. (1981) described an unusual familial cardiomyopathy characterized by aberrant accumulations of desmin-type intermediate filaments.
quotes: An unusual familial cardiomyopathy characterized by aberrant accumulations of desmin-type intermediate filaments.

phenotypes.text: aberrant accumulations of desmin-type intermediate filaments

relevance_reason: The paper reports two unrelated patients with slowly progressive congenital myopathy with cytoplasmic bodies, one of whom also had cardiomyopathy. This matches the historical clinical and pathological descriptions of cytoplasmic body/desmin-related myopathy. No gene or variant was identified.

findings.statement: Wolburg et al. (1982) reported 2 unrelated 32-year-old patients with a congenital, slowly progressive skeletal myopathy. One patient (case 2) also had congenital paresis of the pupillary dilator muscle and cardiomyopathy. The course ended in severe impairment of skeletal muscle function in case 1 but not in case 2.
quotes: Observations on two patients from unrelated families are reported. Both patients were 32 years old and suffered from a congenital affection of the skeletal muscles.
In one (case 2) congenital paresis of the dilator muscle of pupil and cardiomyopathy were also present.
The course of the disease may (case 1) but need not (case 2) terminate in severe impairment of skeletal muscle function.

phenotypes.text: congenital paresis of pupillary dilator muscle

findings.statement: In both patients, Wolburg et al. (1982) found abnormal variation in muscle fiber caliber on muscle biopsy, and in case 1 atrophic fibers were grouped in places. Inclusions with dense granular and fine filamentous components, consistent with cytoplasmic bodies, were present in about one-third of fibers in case 1 and about one-tenth in case 2. The biopsies also showed Z-disk streaming or disintegration and subsarcolemmal pure filamentous bodies.
quotes: In both cases muscle biopsy showed pathologic variations of muscle fiber caliber, and in case 1 atrophic fibers were grouped in some places.
Inclusions consisting of dense granular and fine filamentous components were found in skeletal muscle fibers, in about a third of the fibers in case 1 and in about a tenth of the fibers in case 2.
Surrounding or apart from the inclusions, the streaming of Z disks or their disintegration were observed. In addition, pure filamentous bodies occurred in the subsarcolemmic position in both cases.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
Abnormality of skeletal muscle fiber size

findings.statement: Wolburg et al. (1982) proposed that the disorder is caused by a basic defect in myofilament biosynthesis. They suggested that this defect is presumably triggered by a neurogenic factor that affects the trophic influence of the neuron on the muscle cell.
quotes: A basic defect of myofilament biosynthesis is considered to be the cause of the disorder. It is presumably evoked by a neurogenic factor affecting the trophic influence of the neuron on the muscle cell.

relevance_reason: Clinical report of a three-generation family with cytoplasmic body myopathy presenting with respiratory insufficiency. This is a historical clinical description relevant to desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy. The abstract reports no molecular data.

findings.statement: Chapon et al. (1989) described 3 patients from 3 successive generations of a family who had cytoplasmic body myopathy and presented with respiratory insufficiency. The patients were 72, 45, and 18 years old. Clinical onset was at about 40 years of age in the 2 older patients and at 18 years in the youngest. Serum muscle enzymes and leukocyte maltase activity were normal. Muscle biopsy in all 3 patients showed numerous cytoplasmic (spheroid) bodies within type I muscle fibers.
quotes: Three patients, 72, 45 and 18 years old belonging to 3 successive generations presented with respiratory insufficiency.
The clinical onset was at about 40 years of age in the two older patients and at 18 years in the youngest one.
The muscle biopsy in all three patients showed numerous cytoplasmic (spheroid) bodies within type I muscle fibers.

phenotypes.text: cytoplasmic (spheroid) bodies in type I muscle fibers

findings.statement: Chapon et al. (1989) reported cytoplasmic body myopathy in 3 successive generations of 1 family. They noted that cytoplasmic body myopathy occurring in families has rarely been reported, and that presentation with respiratory insufficiency in adult life is even rarer.
quotes: Three patients, 72, 45 and 18 years old belonging to 3 successive generations presented with respiratory insufficiency.
Familial cytoplasmic body myopathy with familial incidence has rarely been reported and still more rarely has been revealed by respiratory insufficiency in adult life.
